title: Israel sends Phinehas and ten leaders to confront the eastern tribes
speaker: the sons of Israel (the congregation)
recipient: Phinehas son of Eleazar and ten tribal leaders
note: 22:13–15 outside candidate list. Envoys speak ‘thus says the whole congregation’ (22:16); only their warning (ot-joshua-v22-19) is recorded.

title: Balak summons Balaam to curse Israel
speaker: Balak king of Moab (recalled by Joshua)
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
note: Joshua’s covenant recital recalls Balak’s summons (Numbers 22:5–6); link as Additional Scripture, as ot-numbers-v23-7 records another retelling.

title: Israel pledges at Shechem to serve the Lord alone
speaker: the people of Israel
note: Covenant pledge inside X004, whose title covers only Joshua’s charge; compare first-pass P00203 (Exodus 24:3, 7). Could merge with first-pass P00591.

title: Caleb offers his daughter Achsah to whoever captures Debir
speaker: Caleb
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
note: Public challenge with a marriage reward; Othniel takes the city. Same offer at Joshua 15:16 (unrecorded, an S01 candidate): one record citing both.

title: The Lord raises up Ehud as Israel’s deliverer from Moab
speaker: the Lord (narrated)
note: Narrated divine appointment; Israel then sends him with tribute. Othniel’s identical formula (3:9) is also unrecorded: report both or neither.

title: Barak summons Zebulun and Naphtali to Kedesh
speaker: Barak
recipient: the tribes of Zebulun and Naphtali
note: Outside candidate list. Reported muster carrying out Deborah’s order (ot-judges-v4-6); first-pass P00601 noted it unrecorded but proposed only Sisera’s muster.

title: The Lord sends a prophet recalling his warning against Amorite gods
speaker: the Lord through an unnamed prophet
note: The prophet’s sending and oracle begin at 6:8 (‘I brought you up from Egypt’); the record cites only its last verse.

title: The Lord has Gideon dismiss the fearful and sort the drinkers
speaker: the Lord
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
note: Widens first-pass P00610 (7:3–5): 7:2 opens the Lord’s order with its purpose, lest Israel boast ‘My own hand saved me.’

title: Gideon swears blood vengeance and tells Jether to kill the kings
speaker: Gideon
recipient: Zebah and Zalmunna; his son Jether
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
note: 8:19’s oath (‘As the Lord lives… I would not kill you’) is the sentence that the recorded order carries out.

title: Zebah and Zalmunna ask Gideon to strike them down himself
speaker: Zebah and Zalmunna, kings of Midian
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
note: Outside candidate list. Request backed by the saying ‘as the man is, so is his strength’; compare ot-judges-v9-54 and ot-1-samuel-v31-4.

title: The Timnites appoint thirty companions to attend Samson
speaker: the people of Timnah
note: Reported appointment of wedding companions, made out of fear; they become the riddle’s counterparties (14:12–15).

title: Micah installs one of his sons as priest of his shrine
speaker: Micah
note: Outside candidate list. He ‘filled the hand’ (ordained) an unauthorized priest before hiring the Levite (ot-judges-v17-10); recording implies no approval.

title: Micah hires and installs the Levite as his priest
speaker: Micah
note: Outside candidate list (17:12 is context). The offer is recorded; 17:11–12 complete it: Micah ‘filled the Levite’s hand’ and he became his priest.

title: Hannah stays home until Samuel is weaned, with Elkanah’s consent
speaker: Hannah; Elkanah
note: 1:22 holds Hannah’s proposal (not until the child is weaned; then he stays before the Lord) that Elkanah’s recorded reply approves.

title: Eli rebukes his sons for their misconduct
speaker: Eli
note: The rebuke opens at 2:23 (‘Why do you act according to this report?’); first-pass P00672 adds the closing maxim (2:25).

title: The Lord calls the boy Samuel and entrusts him with his word
speaker: the Lord
note: Samuel’s prophetic call; 3:19–21 confirm him as prophet to all Israel. Only Eli’s directions (3:5–6, 3:9, 3:17) are recorded.

title: Saul summons Israel to war with pieces of oxen and a threat
speaker: Saul
note: Call to arms under threat (‘Whoever does not come out after Saul and Samuel—they will do this to his oxen!’); the muster follows (11:8).

title: Samuel asks Israel to testify if he has wronged them
speaker: Samuel
note: 12:4–5 complete the procedure: the people acquit him, and Samuel calls the Lord and his anointed as witnesses (‘Witness’).

title: Saul chooses three thousand men and sends the rest home
speaker: Saul
recipient: three thousand chosen men; the rest of the people
note: Reported selection of a standing army, a thousand placed under Jonathan at Geba; like the appointment in first-pass P00716.

title: Saul sounds the trumpet throughout the land to rally Israel
speaker: Saul
note: Trumpet call after Jonathan’s strike; the people are called out after Saul to Gilgal (13:4). Compare first-pass musters P00609 and P00601.

title: Samuel relays the Lord’s order to strike Amalek
speaker: the Lord through Samuel
note: 15:2 opens the oracle with its ground, Amalek’s ambush on the way from Egypt, executing C1197 (Deuteronomy 25:17–19).

title: Saul sends messengers to seize David, even on his sickbed
speaker: Saul
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
note: 19:14 is the first sending to take David, rebuffed by Michal’s ruse; first-pass P00720 covers the earlier watch order (19:11).

title: Saul sends three bands of messengers to seize David at Naioth
speaker: Saul
note: Reported order given three times; each band prophesies instead, then Saul goes himself (19:22–24). Distinct from 19:11–15.

title: David asks the priest Abimelech for a spear or sword
speaker: David
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
note: Request answered with Goliath’s sword (‘Give it to me’, 21:10); the priest’s offer is only a Study Context record (ot-1-samuel-v21-10).

title: Saul summons Abimelech and all the priests of Nob
speaker: Saul
recipient: Abimelech son of Ahitub and his father’s house
note: Reported summons leading to the massacre ordered at 22:17–18; 22:12 is only a Study Context record.

title: Saul asks David to swear to spare his descendants, and David swears
speaker: Saul; David
note: 24:23 records the oath sworn in reply, as first-pass P00634 extends ot-judges-v15-12 to 15:13.

title: David orders his men to strap on their swords against Nabal
speaker: David
note: ‘Each of you strap on his sword’: four hundred go up while two hundred stay with the baggage; Abigail’s intervention halts them.

title: David swears to leave no male of Nabal’s house alive
speaker: David
note: Rash oath of vengeance, abandoned after Abigail’s plea (25:32–34; AUD-09-25-30); vows are recorded as in first-pass P00623.

title: David sends servants to ask Abigail to become his wife
speaker: David, through his servants
note: Marriage proposal by messengers (‘David has sent us to you to take you as his wife’); Abigail consents and follows them.

title: David sends spies to confirm that Saul has come
speaker: David
note: Reported sending, like ot-joshua-v2-1 (Joshua sends two spies).

title: David asks who will go down with him into Saul’s camp
speaker: David
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
note: Call for a volunteer; Abishai answers, ‘I will enter with you.’

title: David forbids Abishai to strike Saul and takes spear and flask
speaker: Abishai; David
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
note: Widens first-pass P00743 (26:9–11): 26:8 is Abishai’s proposal that the prohibition answers, as 24:5–8 are linked for the cave.

title: The Lord repays each one’s righteousness and faithfulness
speaker: David
note: General maxim grounding David’s restraint toward the Lord’s anointed; compare first-pass P01485 (Greek Psalm 61:13) and P00736 (1 Samuel 24:20).

title: Saul expels the mediums and spiritists from the land
speaker: King Saul
note: Outside candidate list. Narrated royal measure enforcing C0637 and C1074, recalled by the medium (28:9) and broken by Saul himself.

title: Saul asks the summoned Samuel to tell him what to do
speaker: Saul
recipient: Samuel, brought up by the medium
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
note: Request for counsel after God stopped answering; follows the recorded requests to the medium (28:8–13). Samuel answers with judgment.

title: David sends shares of the spoil to the elders of Judah
speaker: David
recipient: the elders of Judah and his allies’ towns
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
note: Gifts sent with a message (‘from the spoils of the Lord’s enemies’), like first-pass envoy commissions P00770 and P00771.

title: David condemns and executes the Amalekite who killed Saul
speaker: David
recipient: the Amalekite; one of his young men
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
note: 1:14 states the charge (raising a hand against the Lord’s anointed) and 1:16 the verdict, ‘Your blood is on your own head.’

title: The men of Judah anoint David king over Judah
speaker: the men of Judah
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
note: Royal anointing at Hebron, which David reports to Jabesh (2:7); compare first-pass P00689 (Samuel anoints Saul).

title: Abner makes Saul’s son Ish-bosheth king over Israel
speaker: Abner son of Ner
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
note: Outside candidate list. Rival installation at Mahanaim; this translation calls him Mephibosheth at 3:7 and 4:8.

title: David demands that Michal be returned to him
speaker: David
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
note: David first sets the condition to Abner (3:13: bring Michal or not see my face); 3:15 reports her being taken from Paltiel.

title: David orders the execution of the murderers of Saul’s son
speaker: David
recipient: Rechab and Baanah; his young men
note: Widens first-pass P00761 (4:11–12), not a second record: the sentence begins with David’s oath at 4:9, citing the Amalekite precedent (4:10).

title: Israel’s elders covenant with David and anoint him king over Israel
speaker: all Israel’s tribes and elders
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
note: AUD-10-5-2 records only the quoted divine word (5:2). Same event as first-pass P00963 (1 Chronicles 11:3): one record citing both.

title: The inhabitants of Jebus tell David he will not enter
speaker: the Jebusites
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
note: Samuel’s account of the same Jebusite taunt (‘You will not come in here’); link as Additional Scripture.

title: Hiram of Tyre sends envoys, cedar and craftsmen to build David’s house
speaker: Hiram king of Tyre
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
note: Envoys sent with builders, like first-pass P00996 (Hiram sends Huram-abi to Solomon); parallel 1 Chronicles 14:1 is also unrecorded.

title: David seeks Saul’s survivors to show kindness and summons Mephibosheth
speaker: King David
note: Keeping his covenant with Jonathan (ot-1-samuel-v20-15); he summons Ziba, then fetches Mephibosheth from Lo-debar. 9:7 is only Study Context.

title: David sends Joab and the whole army against Ammon
speaker: King David
note: Reported dispatch answering Ammon’s hire of Syrian troops; parallel 1 Chronicles 19:8 is unrecorded (an S03 candidate): one record citing both.

title: Hadadezer summons the Syrians from beyond the River
speaker: Hadadezer
recipient: the Syrians beyond the River, under Shobach
note: Reported muster like first-pass P00601 (Sisera); parallel 1 Chronicles 19:16 is an S03 candidate. David’s answering muster (10:17) is narrative.

title: David sends Joab and all Israel to besiege Rabbah
speaker: King David
recipient: Joab, his servants and all Israel
note: Reported dispatch while David stays in Jerusalem, the setting for the orders concerning Bathsheba and Uriah.

title: David sends messengers to inquire about and take Bathsheba
speaker: King David
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
note: Reported orders behind the adultery, before the recorded orders about Uriah (11:6–15); Nathan’s oracle condemns the taking (12:9).

title: David orders Joab to expose Uriah to deadly fighting
speaker: King David
recipient: Joab, by a letter carried by Uriah
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
note: 11:14 reports how the order was delivered: a letter sent by Uriah’s own hand.

title: David sends for the widowed Bathsheba and takes her as wife
speaker: King David
note: Reported summons into marriage after the mourning, judged evil in the Lord’s eyes; compare David’s proposal to Abigail (1 Samuel 25:39–40).

title: The Lord sends Nathan to confront David with a parable
speaker: the Lord
recipient: Nathan the prophet, sent to David
note: First pass noted this commission unrecorded (P00775 covers David’s verdict, 12:5–6). Compare ot-1-kings-v12-23 and ot-isaiah-v22-15.

title: Fast and plead while there is hope; the dead do not return
speaker: David
note: David’s rationale for ending his fast (‘I will go to him, but he will not return to me’); include only if such reflections are itemized.

title: The Lord, through Nathan, names Solomon Jedidiah
speaker: the Lord through Nathan the prophet
note: Divine naming like C0038 (Name Sarah’s son Isaac); this translation renders the name Idedi. The sender could be read as David.

title: Tamar begs Amnon not to send her away
speaker: Tamar
note: Second plea, distinct from ot-2-samuel-v13-12; it echoes the violator’s duty not to send her away (C1141, Deuteronomy 22:29).

title: The woman of Tekoa presses David to bring back his banished son
speaker: the woman of Tekoa
note: The point of Joab’s scripted appeal (ot-2-samuel-v14-2), grounded in the saying that we all die like water spilled on the ground.

title: Absalom demands that Joab arrange an audience with David
speaker: Absalom
note: The demand is first made at 14:29 (Absalom twice sends for Joab, who refuses); 14:32 restates it after the barley is burned.

title: Absalom sends agents to proclaim him king at the trumpet signal
speaker: Absalom
recipient: his secret agents in all Israel’s tribes
note: ‘When you hear the horn’s sound, say, King Absalom has begun to reign in Hebron!’ The order that launches the revolt.

title: Absalom summons Ahithophel, David’s counselor, from his city
speaker: Absalom
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
note: Reported summons during the Hebron sacrifices; Ahithophel’s defection prompts David’s prayer (15:31) and Hushai’s mission (15:34).

title: David leaves ten concubines to keep the palace
speaker: King David
note: Outside candidate list. Reported assignment that sets up Absalom’s act (16:21–22) and their later seclusion (20:3).

title: Ittai swears to stay with David in life or death
speaker: Ittai the Gittite
note: Oath refusing David’s order to turn back (ot-2-samuel-v15-19, v15-20); compare Ruth’s pledge (ot-ruth-v1-16). David lets him cross (15:22).

title: David sends Zadok back with the priests’ sons to bring him word
speaker: King David
recipient: Zadok the priest, with Ahimaaz and Jonathan
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
note: Sets up the courier line that ot-2-samuel-v15-36 relies on; distinct from returning the ark (ot-2-samuel-v15-25).

title: David asks Hushai to return and counter Ahithophel’s advice
speaker: King David
note: 15:33 opens the instruction with its first branch: going with David would make Hushai a burden.

summary: Most passages need nothing; the gaps are narrated orders and commissions in 1–2 Samuel (David anointed at Hebron, Nathan sent, Bathsheba taken, Absalom's revolt orders, Saul's ox summons, 'strap on your swords'), plus extensions to existing records.
